evaluations.note: The fixture has pageable 64 MiB copies, 600 tiny launches, and one strided kernel, so a correct report names at least two of them.
evaluations.prompt: Profile the HIP app in this directory with rocprofv3 (build it with make, run ./app) and tell me where the time goes and what to fix first. Save your summary to profile_summary.md.
expected_behavior: Run rocprofv3 with a tracing option such as --runtime-trace or --kernel-trace on ./app, keeping the default rocpd database output
Summarize the resulting results.db with the skill's analyze_trace.py script instead of hand-parsing CSV files
Report the hot kernels and at least two of: slow pageable host-to-device copies, the launch-bound tiny_kernel, or GPU idle time, each with a concrete code change
unexpected_behavior: Use the deprecated direct --output-format csv as the only output
Report timings or findings that did not come from an actual profiling run

evaluations.note: strided_copy reads with stride 33, so the counters show about 4 KiB of DRAM traffic per memory instruction, a 3% L2 hit rate, and near-peak bandwidth spent on over-fetch.
evaluations.prompt: Use hardware performance counters to find out whether the strided_copy kernel in this HIP app is memory-bound or compute-bound, and why. Build it with make and run ./app. Put your conclusions in counters_report.md.
expected_behavior: Run rocprofv3 with several --pmc groups restricted to strided_copy (for example with --kernel-include-regex), keeping FETCH_SIZE and WRITE_SIZE in separate groups
Summarize the pass_N databases with the skill's analyze_counters.py script

Conclude that strided_copy is memory-bound because of uncoalesced, over-fetching accesses (low L2 hit rate, DRAM bytes per memory instruction far above the coalesced ideal) and recommend making consecutive threads read consecutive addresses
unexpected_behavior: Put FETCH_SIZE and WRITE_SIZE in the same --pmc group
Report GRBM_GUI_ACTIVE / GRBM_COUNT from the counter run as the GPU utilization

Run rocprofv3 on my PyTorch training script on an MI300X and show me which GPU kernels and memory copies dominate one training step.
What is the wave occupancy and L2 cache hit rate of my HIP gemm kernel on MI300X? I'd like actual hardware counter numbers.

I have a rocprofv3 results.db from last week's run. List the ten longest kernels and how much time went to host-to-device copies.

Analyze this PyTorch profiler trace JSON from my training run and write a report on GPU kernel efficiency.
Capture an Nsight Systems timeline of my CUDA application on an NVIDIA H100.
